text:
Maya: FYI — competitor rolled out a low-cost tier that's getting noisy with customers asking if we can match price. Want a quick sync on scope + launch gating. Thoughts?
Juan: Seen the spec, it looks like they trade quality for latency/cost via aggressive quantization and smaller context sizes.
Alek: Engineering note — building a ‘cheap’ variant isn't trivial: quantization, different kernel path, and separate perf profiles. Estimate a 3–4 sprint spike + 2 sprints to make autoscaling reliable.
Olivia: Sales already fielding asks from a couple pilots. They want: 1) cheaper price tier, 2) clear SLOs, 3) a fallback plan if quality drops.
Maya: Proposed options: (A) Feature parity-ish: match price across text gen & embeddings (big effort); (B) Scoped MVP: cheaper tier limited to embeddings + short-form generation + non-sensitive workloads; (C) Product-led positioning: keep quality-first and introduce cost controls (batching, routing) for customers who *need* lower unit cost.
Sam: +1 for Scoped MVP (B) — minimizes risk and buys us time to see if this competitor really moves demand.
sre-bot: Deploy bot: reminder — any new tier requires adding per-route throttles and per-tenant cost telemetry before GA.
Juan: For (B) specifics: embeddings + 256-token gen max, quantized int8 weights, disabled function-calling, disabled streaming. That cuts perf surface and exposure to hallucinations.
Alek: If we go (B), we should gate by: 1) per-route tail latency < 200ms p95 on dedicated pools, 2) cost per 1M tokens < $X (benchmarked), 3) auto-fallback to standard model when quality/regression alerts trigger.
Olivia: Also require clear sales messaging: "intended for high-throughput non-sensitive workloads" — no private deployment on day 1. Customers in regulated sectors will expect on-prem or VPC; don't promise that.
Maya: Launch checklist draft: must-haves (SLOs met in perf test, autoscale configured, fallback behavior tested, docs + warning labels, marketing copy cleared), nice-to-haves (canary with 5 existing low-risk customers, per-tenant budget caps, improved evals for short-form).
Sam: Metrics to watch during canary: per-tenant error rate, hallucination regressions on our short-form eval set, unit cost, and fallback frequency.
Alek: Ops ask — we need a routing policy that prefers cheaper pool but transparently falls back if p95 latency degrades or KV cache miss rate spikes. I can prototype the policy in a day if PMs sign off.
Juan: Risk: quantization may surface new failure modes for certain topologies; require a model-level regression gate with model-specific eval prompts before enabling per-customer.
Olivia: Sales consequence — we need an explicit SLA sheet for the cheaper tier (lower availability & no enterprise compliance). Otherwise legal will flag it.
Maya: Decision propose: go with (B) Scoped MVP, limit to embeddings + short-form non-sensitive text gen. Canary to 5 customers. No Private/Dedicated in initial GA. Launch criteria = Alek's gates + canary stable for 2 weeks.
Sam: Timeline ask: can we aim for a beta in 6 weeks?
Alek: Tight but doable if we treat it as a parallel spike: week 1–2 quantization + kernel selection spike; week 3 routing + fallback; week 4 perf tuning; week 5 docs + canary setup; week 6 canary. Need 2 engineers + 0.5 SRE + model ops support.
Maya: I'll send out a PRD with the proposed launch criteria and assignees. Action items: Alek to prototype routing policy, Juan to define eval prompts & regression gate, Olivia to draft sales/marketing caveats, Sam to coordinate canary customers.
Olivia: I'll pre-clear one pilot with ACME corp (non-sensitive analytics use).
Juan: I'll start building the short-form eval harness today and post results in #eng-ml.
Alek: Will start the routing prototype tomorrow.
Maya: Thanks — let's reconvene Wed 10am to lock scope and approve PRD. :thumbsup:
